evals.prompt: Add Rectangle, the macOS window manager, to the installer's catalog. Research it, decide how it installs and uninstalls, and write the entry with its verification comment.
evals.expected_output: A [[tool]] block for a vendor-macOS-only app with one cask method that places the bundle in ~/Applications, a dated # Verified comment citing the research, the absence of a CLI recorded so no link is promised, the id added to MACOS_ONLY in tests/test_registry.py with the vendor fact, and the first-run dialogs written as a UAT line deferred to the owner's Mac.
assertions: The block carries a dated `# Verified` comment above `[[tool]]` that cites the vendor page or release listing the agent read, not a recollection
There is exactly one `cask` method with `os`, `cask` and `app` params, plus `min_os_version` when the cask needs one, and the bundle lands in `~/Applications` through the executor's `--appdir`
The `# Verified` comment records that Rectangle ships no CLI, so no `~/.local/bin` link applies, and records any other platform gap it finds instead of promising one
The id is added to `MACOS_ONLY` in `tests/test_registry.py` together with the vendor fact that no Linux build exists, so the exemption has a reason
First-run dialogs are not marked passed: the agent writes a UAT line deferred to the owner's Mac and names the Gatekeeper prompt as expected once per fresh cask install

evals.prompt: hey, can you add the Rio terminal to the catalog? it runs on macOS and Linux. pick the install method and set up the terminal defaults for it
evals.expected_output: A registry entry for the terminal and its row in references/terminal-defaults.md in the same change, every rule cell starting with a status word, the four defaults applied as rules and never offered as questions, and the skill's test file passing.
assertions: The agent reads `references/terminal-defaults.md` at step 7 and adds the new terminal's row there in the same change as its registry entry, not in SKILL.md
Each of the four rule cells in the new row starts with one status word (`vendor`, `written`, `planned (phase N)`, `gap (backlog 999.x)`, `n/a` or `unverified`) followed by its reason

The agent applies the four terminal defaults as rules and never asks the developer whether to enable word navigation, clear or same-directory behavior; only extras such as shell integration are offered
The agent never writes the global Option-as-Alt switch for word navigation and binds only the two Option+Left and Option+Right chords where the vendor default does not already meet the rule
`uv run pytest tests/test_tool_onboarding_skill.py` is run and passes, and the agent does not claim a real-Mac check passed

evals.prompt:
the entry below only has a macOS cask, but the vendor ships Linux builds as well. tell me what to change and update its notes.

```toml
# Verified 2026-11-01: cask only
[[tool]]
id = "example-desk"
name = "Example Desk"
category = "dev"
cmd = "example-desk"
priority = "P3"
audience = "human"
tier = "user"
verified = 2026-11-01
desc = "Example desktop tool."

[[tool.method]]
kind = "cask"
os = ["macos"]
cask = "example-desk"
app = "Example Desk.app"
```
evals.expected_output: A review that opens a ### Phase 999.x item under ## Backlog in .planning/ROADMAP.md naming the missing Linux capability, keeps the id in a gap set of tests/test_registry.py (adding a NO_LINUX set when none fits) with that item named, refreshes the # Verified comment, and never calls the entry macOS-only.
assertions: The review opens a `### Phase 999.x` item under `## Backlog` in `.planning/ROADMAP.md` that names the missing Linux capability, instead of only describing the gap in prose

The id stays in a gap set (`NO_*`) of `tests/test_registry.py` (a new `NO_LINUX` set when none fits, never `MACOS_ONLY`) with that backlog item named next to it, so the gap stays visible until it closes
Neither the entry, its `# Verified` comment nor the answer labels the tool macOS-only, because the vendor ships Linux builds and the missing method is this installer's gap
The `# Verified` comment is updated with a new date and says which method is missing on which OS and why
The agent walks steps 3, 4b and 8 against the existing block and checks that install, ownership and removal still give truthful answers
